content.value_statement: Testing work often spans frameworks, test levels, and release gates. This skill organizes QA planning, automation prompts, and verification steps for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
actual_capabilities: Outlines test strategy, framework selection, coverage planning, and CI setup steps.
Breaks QA work into unit, integration, E2E, browser automation, performance, review, and quality gate phases.
Provides copy-paste prompts for related testing and review skills.
Lists a quality gate checklist for coverage, passing tests, benchmarks, security scans, reviews, and linting.
Shows a simple testing pyramid model for balancing test coverage.
limitations: It is a workflow guide, not an executable test runner.
It depends on separate named skills for implementation details.
It does not include framework-specific test code or repository configuration.
It does not verify results unless the user runs the recommended tools.

use_cases.title: Plan Release Testing
use_cases.description: Define test coverage, quality gates, and verification steps before a production release.

use_cases.title: Build Automation Coverage
use_cases.description: Organize unit, integration, API, browser, and E2E test work across a repository.

use_cases.title: Standardize QA Reviews
use_cases.description: Create repeatable checklists for code review, linting, security scans, and final acceptance.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Test Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for a small feature.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to plan a testing strategy for my feature. Include unit, integration, E2E, browser, and quality gate steps.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Release Checklist
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to create a QA checklist for a release candidate. Include test ownership, coverage goals, automation scope, and verification steps.

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate Automation Work
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to coordinate test automation across JavaScript, Python, API, browser, performance, and code review work for this repository.

prompt_templates.title: Design CI Quality Gates
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design a CI quality gate workflow that combines unit tests, integration tests, E2E coverage, performance checks, security scanning, and final verification.

output_examples.input: Create a QA plan for a new checkout flow.
output: Testing scope is separated into unit, integration, E2E, browser, performance, and security review tasks.
Quality gates include coverage, passing tests, E2E paths, benchmarks, security scan results, review approval, and clean linting.

output_examples.input: Prepare browser automation guidance for a responsive web app.
output: Browser automation work covers headless setup, visual testing, screenshot capture, and responsive design checks.
The plan recommends using existing browser testing skills with repository-specific user journeys and test data.

output_examples.input: Set up a release readiness checklist.
output_examples.output: The result is a concise checklist covering coverage targets, passing tests, E2E coverage, performance benchmarks, security scans, review approval, and lint status.

best_practices: Start with the test strategy phase before writing detailed automation prompts.
Map each quality gate to a clear owner and measurable pass condition.
Use repository-specific context and existing test framework choices.
anti_patterns: Skipping unit and integration coverage while adding only E2E tests.
Using screenshot prompts on sensitive production data.
Treating the checklist as proof of quality without running the tests.

faq.question: Does this skill run tests for me?
faq.answer: No. It organizes QA work and prompts. You still need to run the selected test tools.

faq.question: Which test levels does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers unit, integration, E2E, browser automation, performance, review, and quality gate phases.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The marketplace metadata lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.

faq.question: Does it include framework-specific examples?
faq.answer: It references JavaScript, Python, API, and browser testing skills, but it does not provide detailed test code.

faq.question: Is this useful for CI planning?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes CI setup, coverage goals, linting, security scans, and release quality gates.

faq.question: What should I provide before using it?
faq.answer: Provide the repository context, target feature, test framework choices, release risks, and current quality requirements.
